# Page 4^page=4
The Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) held its 59th meeting from February 4 to 6, 2026, under the chairmanship of Shri Sanjay Malhotra, Governor, Reserve Bank of India. The MPC members Dr. Nagesh Kumar, Shri Saugata Bhattacharya, Prof. Ram Singh, Dr. Poonam Gupta and Shri Indranil Bhattacharyya attended the meeting. Monetary Policy Statement, 2025-26 Resolution of the Monetary Policy Committee February 4 to 6, 2026 After a detailed assessment of the evolving macroeconomic and financial developments and the outlook, the MPC voted unanimously to keep the policy repo rate under the liquidity adjustment facility (LAF) unchanged. The MPC also decided to continue with the neutral stance. SDF Rate 5.00% Repo Rate 5.25% MSF Rate & Bank Rate 5.50%

# Page 5^page=5
Growth Outlook As per the First Advance Estimates, real GDP is projected to grow by 7.4% (y-o-y) in 2025-26, led by strong private consumption and fixed investment. Net external demand remained a drag as imports exceeded exports. On the supply side, real GVA growth of 7.3% is supported by a buoyant services sector, resilient agriculture, and a revival in manufacturing. ➢ Consumption outlook: Private consumption expected to be supported by buoyant services, GST rationalisation, healthy rabi prospects, monetary easing, and benign inflation. ➢ Investment outlook: Investment activity likely to maintain momentum, aided by high capacity utilisation, conducive financial conditions, strong balance sheets of banks and corporates, robust credit growth, and the Government’s continued capex push. Robust domestic demand is likely to attract fresh investments by the private sector Services exports are expected to remain strong, merchandise exports will get a boost from the prospective trade deal with the US. ➢ External sector: Trade pact with the EU coupled with trade deals with New Zealand and Oman expected to diversify exports and strengthen the external sector. ➢ Risks: Geopolitical tensions, global trade uncertainty, and volatility in financial markets and int commodity prices pose downside risks. ➢ Growth outlook: Real GDP growth for 2026-27 revised up to 6.9% in Q1 and 7.0% in Q2.

# Page 6^page=6
Growth Outlook ➢ Growth outlook: Real GDP growth for 2026-27 revised up to 6.9% in Q1 and 7.0% in Q2.

# Page 7^page=7
Inflation Outlook Headline CPI inflation remained low at 0.7% in November and 1.3% in December, 2025. While food group continued to be in deflation, inflation within the fuel group remained moderate in November and December. Core inflation (CPI excluding food and fuel) too remained benign, despite the pick up in prices of precious metals. Excluding gold, core inflation remained stable at 2.6% in December. ➢ Near-term outlook: Food inflation likely to remain benign due to healthy kharif production, adequate foodgrain buffers and favourable rabi sowing. ➢ Upside risks to inflation: Geopolitical uncertainty coupled with volatility in energy prices, possible volatility from precious metals prices and adverse weather events. ➢ Projections: CPI inflation at 2.1% in 2025-26. ➢ Overall assessment: Underlying inflation pressures (excluding precious metals) remain muted.

# Page 8^page=8
Rationale for Monetary Policy Decisions On the growth front, economic activity remains resilient. The First Advance Estimates suggest continuing growth momentum, driven by domestic factors amidst a challenging external environment. The growth outlook remains favourable. Based on a comprehensive review of the domestic macroeconomic conditions and the outlook, the MPC is of the view that the current policy rate is appropriate. Accordingly, the MPC voted to continue with the existing policy rate. The MPC also agreed to retain the neutral stance.
